overview: This Senate resolution sets the budget for the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (often called HELP), which handles health care, schools, workplace rules, and retirement plans, from March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2027, the two-year span of the current Congress. It lets the committee spend money from the Senate's internal operating account, hire staff, and, with permission, borrow employees from federal agencies. It caps spending at $7,767,027 for March through September 2025, $13,314,904 for the 2026 budget year, and $5,547,877 for October 2026 through February 2027, about $26.6 million in all, with smaller set-asides for outside consultants and staff training. Every Senate committee gets a resolution like this at the start of each Congress, and the amounts are usually combined into one larger funding resolution. As of February 12, 2025, it had been sent to the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, which reviews committee budgets.
for: Supporters say committees need a predictable budget for staff and investigations so they can hold hearings, write legislation, and keep watch over the federal agencies in their area.
against: Critics say committee budgets get little public scrutiny and that the Senate should look harder for savings in its own operating costs before approving these amounts.
